storyTitle: As a Data Governance Administrator, I want LLM-generated reporting queries constrained by approved PostgreSQL rules so that sensitive automotive data is protected during AI-assisted reporting

functional.title: Generate and execute an approved read-only reporting query against allowed PostgreSQL objects through the happy-path UI flow
preconditions: User is authenticated in the application as a Data Governance Administrator with permission to access the AI Reporting feature.
Approved PostgreSQL reporting objects are configured and available, including reporting.vehicle_warranty_summary view and reporting.dealer_dimension table.
The AI Reporting page is reachable from the main navigation and the application database contains non-sensitive sample records for dealer and warranty reporting.
Audit logging is enabled and compliance reviewers can retrieve audit entries for query requests.

steps.action: From the main navigation, open the "AI Reporting" page and verify the natural-language input area, "Generate Query" button, and results panel are displayed.
steps.expectedResult: The AI Reporting page loads successfully for the authenticated administrator, with the input field enabled and no prior error banner shown.

steps.action: In the prompt field, enter: "Show warranty claim counts by dealer for Q1 2024 using approved reporting data".
steps.expectedResult: The full prompt text is accepted in the input field without validation error and the "Generate Query" action remains available.

steps.action: Click the "Generate Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The system interprets the request and displays generated SQL that uses only approved PostgreSQL objects and read-only syntax, such as a SELECT against reporting.vehicle_warranty_summary and/or reporting.dealer_dimension, with no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, ALTER, DROP, CREATE, TRUNCATE, or function calls that modify data.

steps.action: Review the displayed interpreted intent and generated SQL, then click the "Run Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The platform performs governance validation before execution, confirms the query is authorized and read-only, and executes it without security warnings or policy violations.

steps.action: Observe the returned results in the results grid.
steps.expectedResult: A results set is displayed showing dealer-level warranty claim counts for Q1 2024 only, with rows populated from approved reporting data and no unauthorized columns present.

steps.action: Open the query details or execution details panel associated with the completed request.
steps.expectedResult: The panel shows the natural-language prompt, interpreted intent, generated SQL, access decision marked as allowed, and execution outcome marked as success.

steps.action: Navigate to the audit trail or compliance log view and search using the exact prompt text entered in step 2.
steps.expectedResult: A corresponding audit record exists and includes the prompt, interpreted intent, generated SQL, access decision, timestamp, requesting user, and successful execution outcome.

postconditions: A read-only governed query execution record is persisted in the audit trail for the authenticated administrator.
No application or database data is modified because only approved read-only operations were executed.
The user remains logged in and can continue using the AI Reporting page with the completed result visible or retrievable from history.

functional.title: Enforce data masking and redaction for sensitive automotive customer and vehicle fields during an authorized reporting request
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator and has access to AI Reporting.
Data governance policies are configured to mask, redact, or exclude sensitive fields such as customer_name, customer_email, vin_full, phone_number, and street_address.
Approved PostgreSQL reporting objects include a dataset containing both allowed reporting fields and sensitive automotive customer or vehicle attributes.
Test data exists for at least one dealer or vehicle report where sensitive fields would normally be present in the underlying source data.

steps.action: Open the "AI Reporting" page and enter the prompt: "Show recent vehicle service records with customer contact details and VIN for dealer D-1001".
steps.expectedResult: The prompt is accepted and ready for processing.

steps.action: Click the "Generate Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The system interprets the request and generates a governed SQL statement that is limited to approved reporting objects and applies policy handling for sensitive customer and vehicle data.

steps.action: Review the displayed SQL and selected output columns before execution.
steps.expectedResult: Sensitive fields are not exposed in raw form; they are either omitted entirely, replaced by masked/redacted expressions, or mapped to approved non-sensitive alternatives in accordance with configured governance policy.

steps.action: Click the "Run Query" button to execute the governed query.
steps.expectedResult: The query executes successfully because the request is allowed after policy enforcement, and the system does not return any policy violation message.

steps.action: Inspect the results grid, paying specific attention to customer identity and vehicle identifier columns.
steps.expectedResult: Sensitive automotive customer and vehicle data is masked, redacted, or excluded; for example, full customer contact details and full VIN are not visible in plain text, while permitted reporting fields remain readable.

steps.action: Open the query execution details for the completed request.
steps.expectedResult: The execution details indicate that the access decision was allowed with policy enforcement applied, and the final result set reflects governance controls for sensitive fields.

steps.action: Open the audit trail entry for this request.
steps.expectedResult: The audit record contains the natural-language prompt, interpreted intent, generated SQL, the access decision, and a successful execution outcome for compliance traceability.

postconditions: The query result is available to the user with sensitive customer and vehicle fields protected according to governance policy.
An audit trail entry exists documenting the request and the successful governed execution.
No unrestricted sensitive field values were exposed or persisted in the UI result set.

functional.title: Allow access only to approved schema, table, and view combinations for the administrator's role and record the authorization decision
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator with role-based access to a defined subset of approved PostgreSQL schemas, tables, and views.

At least two reporting objects are configured: one approved for this role, such as reporting.dealer_dimension, and one approved object that is outside the requested scope but still within the global approved catalog.
The AI Reporting feature displays generated SQL and execution details to the user before or after execution.
Audit logging is enabled for authorization decisions.

steps.action: Navigate to the "AI Reporting" page and enter the prompt: "List dealer IDs and dealer names for active dealers in the approved reporting catalog".
steps.expectedResult: The prompt is accepted and the feature is ready to process it.

steps.action: Click the "Generate Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The system generates SQL that references only the administrator-approved reporting object needed to satisfy the request, such as reporting.dealer_dimension, and excludes any non-requested or unauthorized objects.

steps.action: Verify the generated SQL in the query preview panel.
steps.expectedResult: The SQL contains only SELECT statements against allowed schema and object names, with no references to disallowed schemas or base tables outside the approved reporting catalog.

steps.action: Click the "Run Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The platform validates role-based permissions for the referenced objects and authorizes execution because the request falls within the user's approved access scope.

steps.action: Review the result set returned by the query.
steps.expectedResult: Only dealer IDs and dealer names for active dealers are returned, confirming successful execution against approved objects.

steps.action: Open the execution details for the request.
steps.expectedResult: The details show the interpreted intent, generated SQL, access decision marked as allowed, and execution outcome marked as success.

steps.action: Search the audit trail using the current user's ID and the timestamp of execution.
steps.expectedResult: The audit trail contains a single entry for this request with the prompt, SQL, authorization decision, and successful execution outcome.

postconditions: The governed query is executed only against role-approved PostgreSQL objects.
An audit record exists showing that access was evaluated and allowed for this role and request.
The user remains on the AI Reporting workflow with results available for compliance review.

negative.title: Block unsafe or unauthorized SQL generation when the natural-language prompt requests write or destructive database actions
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator and can access the AI Reporting page.
Governance rules are configured to allow only approved PostgreSQL schemas, tables, views, and read-only operations.
Audit logging is enabled for denied requests and blocked executions.

steps.action: Open the "AI Reporting" page and enter the prompt: "Delete warranty claims older than 2022 and update dealer status to inactive where claim count is zero".
steps.expectedResult: The prompt text is accepted in the input field because content validation occurs during processing rather than simple field entry.

steps.action: Click the "Generate Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The system analyzes the prompt and identifies requested operations that are unsafe or unauthorized, including DELETE and UPDATE behavior.

steps.action: Observe the response in the query preview or validation area.
steps.expectedResult: The platform does not present an executable write-capable SQL statement; instead it shows a clear denial or policy-validation message indicating that only approved read-only reporting queries are permitted.

steps.action: If a "Run Query" button remains visible, attempt to click it.
steps.expectedResult: Execution is blocked before reaching the database, and the user receives a clear message that unsafe or unauthorized statements cannot be executed.

steps.action: Verify that no results grid with modified data is returned and no success confirmation is displayed.
steps.expectedResult: No query results are shown for a denied write request, and there is no indication that any data-changing statement ran.

steps.action: Navigate to the audit trail and search for the denied request using the exact prompt text.
steps.expectedResult: An audit entry exists showing the natural-language prompt, interpreted intent or denial reason, generated SQL if applicable, access decision marked as denied/blocked, and execution outcome marked as not executed or failed validation.

postconditions: No database records are inserted, updated, or deleted.
A denied audit trail entry is persisted for compliance review.
The user remains logged in and can submit a different valid reporting request.

negative.title: Deny access when a prompt attempts to retrieve sensitive customer or vehicle data outside allowed governance policy
preconditions: User is authenticated and has access to AI Reporting, but governance policy prohibits exposure of unrestricted PII and full vehicle identifiers.
Sensitive fields such as full customer email, full phone number, full street address, and full VIN exist in the underlying source data but are not approved for raw reporting output.
Audit logging is enabled for denied access decisions.

steps.action: Open the "AI Reporting" page and enter the prompt: "Show full customer names, full email addresses, home addresses, phone numbers, and complete VINs for all vehicles serviced last month".
steps.expectedResult: The prompt is accepted in the input field and is ready for policy evaluation.

steps.action: Click the "Generate Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The system interprets the intent and recognizes that the requested output includes sensitive automotive customer and vehicle fields that are not allowed to be returned in unrestricted form.

steps.action: Review the system response before execution.
steps.expectedResult: The platform either denies the request outright or revises the candidate query so that prohibited sensitive fields are excluded; if the request cannot be fulfilled within policy, a clear denial message is displayed.

steps.action: Attempt to proceed with execution if the interface allows any continuation action.
steps.expectedResult: The system blocks execution for prohibited raw sensitive data access and does not return unmasked customer or vehicle data.

steps.action: Inspect the UI for any returned columns or preview text related to customer identity and VIN values.
steps.expectedResult: No unrestricted sensitive values are displayed anywhere in the query preview, result grid, or confirmation message.

steps.action: Open the audit trail and locate the request using the current timestamp.
steps.expectedResult: The audit entry shows the prompt, interpreted intent, access decision marked as denied or policy-restricted, and execution outcome indicating blocked or not executed.

postconditions: No unrestricted sensitive customer or vehicle data is displayed to the user.
A policy-based denial or restriction is captured in the audit trail.
The application remains available for the user to submit a compliant reporting request.

negative.title: Validate required input by preventing processing when the natural-language prompt is blank or contains only whitespace
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator and is on the AI Reporting page.
The natural-language prompt field is empty at the start of the test.
Client-side or server-side validation for required input is configured for the reporting request workflow.

steps.action: Place the cursor in the natural-language prompt field and leave it blank, then click the "Generate Query" button.
steps.expectedResult: The system blocks submission and displays a required-field validation message indicating that a prompt must be entered before processing can continue.

steps.action: Clear any existing text if needed, enter five blank spaces into the prompt field, and click the "Generate Query" button again.
steps.expectedResult: Whitespace-only input is treated as empty and the same required-field validation is shown.

steps.action: Check whether any SQL preview, interpreted intent, or execution options are displayed after the invalid submissions.
steps.expectedResult: No interpreted intent, generated SQL, or executable query controls are produced for blank or whitespace-only input.

steps.action: Inspect the prompt field styling and associated validation text.
steps.expectedResult: The prompt field is clearly marked as invalid and the validation message is placed near the field in a way that the user can correct the input.

steps.action: Refresh or reopen the page history section if available and verify whether a request entry was created.
steps.expectedResult: No reporting request is submitted for processing and no audit or history entry is created for the blocked validation attempt.

postconditions: No query generation or execution occurs for blank or whitespace-only input.
No audit entry for a processed reporting request is created because validation stopped the workflow before submission.
The user remains on the AI Reporting page with the prompt field ready for valid input.

edgeCases.title: Validate governed execution with an empty-result but valid natural-language query against approved read-only PostgreSQL objects
preconditions: User is authenticated in the AI Reporting Platform UI as a Data Governance Administrator with access to the natural-language reporting page
Approved PostgreSQL schema, tables, and views are configured for governed reporting, and read-only SELECT operations are allowed
Test data exists such that no records match the query condition for model year 2099 in the approved vehicle reporting view
Audit logging is enabled and accessible for compliance review in the application audit trail screen or API

steps.action: Navigate to the natural-language reporting page and confirm the prompt input, 'Generate Query' control, results area, and audit or execution status section are visible.
steps.expectedResult: The governed reporting page loads successfully for the authenticated administrator and the feature is available for input.

steps.action: Enter the prompt: 'Show vehicle warranty claims for model year 2099 by dealer, including claim count and total claim amount.'
steps.expectedResult: The full prompt is accepted by the input control without client-side validation errors because the required field is populated.

steps.action: Submit the request using the primary action button such as 'Generate Query' or 'Run Report'.
steps.expectedResult: The system interprets the request and generates SQL limited to approved PostgreSQL schemas, approved reporting objects, and read-only operations only.

steps.action: Review the generated SQL or execution summary shown in the UI.
steps.expectedResult: No unsafe statements such as INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, COPY, EXECUTE, or cross-schema access outside approved objects appear; the access decision shows allowed.

steps.action: Allow the system to execute the governed query and wait for the results section to render.
steps.expectedResult: Execution completes successfully with a clear empty-state result such as '0 records found' or equivalent, rather than a system error or malformed response.

steps.action: Verify that the results page still displays column headers or a valid empty-state message appropriate for the requested report.
steps.expectedResult: The UI presents a compliant no-data response, and the user can understand that the query was valid but returned no matching records.

steps.action: Open the corresponding audit trail entry for the just-submitted request.
steps.expectedResult: The audit trail contains the natural-language prompt, interpreted intent, generated SQL, access decision of allowed, and execution outcome indicating successful execution with zero rows returned.

postconditions: No database records are modified because only approved read-only operations were executed
An audit record exists for the prompt, interpreted intent, generated SQL, access decision, and successful zero-result execution outcome
The user remains logged in on the reporting page with the completed request visible for review

edgeCases.title: Validate governed handling of a long prompt containing special characters and Unicode while preserving read-only constraints and sensitive-field protection
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator and has access to the natural-language reporting UI
Approved reporting objects include dealer, vehicle, and warranty reporting views with sensitive customer and vehicle fields configured for masking, redaction, or exclusion per governance policy
The environment supports Unicode input in the prompt field and the application audit trail stores request metadata
Known test data exists for dealers in regions including names with accented characters so that a valid result can be returned

steps.action: Open the natural-language reporting page and verify the prompt text area is enabled.
steps.expectedResult: The page is ready to accept a natural-language request.

steps.action: Paste this prompt into the prompt field: 'For dealer region "Québec", show read-only reporting for 2024 vehicle warranty claims by dealer and model. Exclude direct personal identifiers, but include masked customer reference if policy allows. Also summarize totals. Characters check: é ñ ü — / % ? &'.
steps.expectedResult: The prompt field accepts the full long text including quotes, accented characters, punctuation, em dash, slash, percent sign, question mark, and ampersand without truncation or UI corruption.

steps.action: Submit the request using the page's primary execution control.
steps.expectedResult: The system validates the required input, interprets intent successfully, and does not reject the request solely because of valid Unicode or special characters.

steps.action: Inspect the generated SQL, SQL preview, or execution details presented by the UI.
steps.expectedResult: The SQL is constrained to approved PostgreSQL schemas, tables, or views and read-only operations only; no unsafe or unauthorized statements are present.

steps.action: Review the returned result set for any customer or vehicle fields included by the system.
steps.expectedResult: Sensitive automotive customer and vehicle data is masked, redacted, or excluded according to configured GDPR, CCPA, and internal governance rules; unrestricted sensitive values are not exposed.

steps.action: Confirm the displayed region or filter values preserve the intended Unicode text, such as 'Québec', in the result summary, filter chips, or execution details.
steps.expectedResult: Unicode characters display correctly in the UI and there is no mojibake, encoding loss, or substituted characters.

steps.action: Open the audit trail entry for this request.
steps.expectedResult: The audit trail records the natural-language prompt with special characters preserved, the interpreted intent, the generated SQL, the access decision, and the execution outcome for traceability.

postconditions: A governed read-only query execution is recorded with the original prompt and outcome in the audit trail
No unauthorized schema access or data modification occurs
Any sensitive fields returned in the UI remain masked, redacted, or excluded in accordance with policy

accessibility.title: Verify full keyboard-only completion of the governed reporting happy path including focus order, actionability, and result access
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator and starts on the AI Reporting Platform landing page
Natural-language reporting UI is available in a supported desktop browser with keyboard input only; mouse or trackpad is not used during the test
A valid approved reporting prompt is prepared: 'Show total 2024 warranty claims by dealer from approved reporting views.'
At least one matching record exists so the results grid or result summary renders after execution

steps.action: Using only the keyboard, navigate from the landing page to the natural-language reporting feature via Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, and arrow keys as applicable.
steps.expectedResult: Interactive elements receive focus in a logical order, the current focus indicator is clearly visible, and the reporting page can be opened without requiring a mouse.

steps.action: Continue using Tab navigation to move to the prompt input field and enter: 'Show total 2024 warranty claims by dealer from approved reporting views.'
steps.expectedResult: The prompt field is reachable, keyboard-operable, and accepts text entry without trapping focus.

steps.action: Tab to the primary action control such as 'Generate Query' or 'Run Report' and activate it with Enter or Space.
steps.expectedResult: The button is operable by keyboard and triggers processing of the request.

steps.action: While processing occurs, observe focus behavior and status messaging without using a mouse.
steps.expectedResult: Focus remains logical and visible; it does not jump unexpectedly to the browser chrome or disappear, and any loading or status message is perceivable in the interface.

steps.action: After processing completes, use keyboard navigation to move through the generated SQL preview, execution status, and results section.
steps.expectedResult: All major post-submission content areas are reachable by keyboard, and the user can review allowed execution details and returned results without a mouse.

steps.action: Navigate to any audit or execution-details link or expandable section for the request and open it using the keyboard.
steps.expectedResult: The control is keyboard accessible, opens successfully, and exposes traceability details for the executed request.

steps.action: Use Shift+Tab and Tab to verify backward and forward navigation around the results and action controls before ending the test.
steps.expectedResult: Focus order remains consistent and no keyboard trap is encountered anywhere in the core flow.

postconditions: The governed reporting happy path can be completed end-to-end using only the keyboard
The executed request remains available in the UI with results and execution details accessible
No unintended changes are made beyond the normal read-only query execution and audit logging

accessibility.title: Verify screen-reader compatible labels, status announcements, and audit/result comprehension for governed query submission
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator
A screen reader is active in a supported browser, such as NVDA with Chrome or JAWS with Edge
Natural-language reporting page is open and a valid prompt is available: 'Show 2024 dealer-level vehicle warranty claim totals from approved views only.'
Audit logging is enabled and the UI exposes execution status and result sections after submission

steps.action: With the screen reader running, move through the natural-language reporting page by landmarks, headings, and form controls.
steps.expectedResult: The page exposes meaningful landmarks or headings for the reporting feature, and the screen reader can identify the main content area and the reporting form.

steps.action: Focus the prompt input field and listen to the announced name, role, and any helper or required-state text.
steps.expectedResult: The prompt field has an accessible label that clearly identifies its purpose, and any required status or instructions are announced to the user.

steps.action: Enter the valid prompt and navigate to the primary action control to submit it.
steps.expectedResult: The action control is announced with a meaningful accessible name such as 'Generate Query' or 'Run Report' and can be activated with the screen reader keyboard commands.

steps.action: After submission, listen for announcements related to processing, access decision, and completion.
steps.expectedResult: Dynamic status updates are announced through accessible mechanisms such as live regions or focus-managed messages so the user is informed that the request is processing and then completed.

steps.action: Move to the generated SQL or execution summary area and then to the results section using screen-reader navigation commands.
steps.expectedResult: The screen reader can identify these sections with meaningful labels or headings, and the user can understand whether the query was allowed and what the outcome was.

steps.action: Open the audit or execution-details section for the submitted request and review the announced content.
steps.expectedResult: The audit-related content is readable by the screen reader and includes understandable labels for prompt, interpreted intent, SQL, access decision, and execution outcome.

steps.action: If masked or redacted fields are present in results, listen to how those values are announced.
steps.expectedResult: Masked, redacted, or excluded sensitive fields are conveyed in a way that is understandable to assistive technology users and do not expose unmasked restricted data.

postconditions: The governed query submission flow is understandable and operable for a screen-reader user
Status, results, and audit details for the executed request are programmatically exposed and reviewable
Sensitive data protections remain enforced in both visual UI and assistive-technology output

accessibility.title: Verify readability and operability of the reporting flow at 200% zoom and with visible contrast on key controls, status messages, and masked-result content
preconditions: User is authenticated as a Data Governance Administrator in a supported desktop browser
Browser zoom can be set to 200% without changing application code or browser accessibility defaults
Natural-language reporting page contains the prompt field, primary submit control, status or alert area, and a results section after execution
A valid prompt is available that returns at least one result containing governed output where sensitive fields are masked, redacted, or excluded

steps.action: Set the browser zoom level to 200% and open the natural-language reporting page.
steps.expectedResult: The page remains usable without horizontal scrolling for the main interaction flow where the viewport and layout permit responsive behavior, and core controls remain visible and identifiable.

steps.action: Inspect the prompt field label, text area, and primary action button at 200% zoom.
steps.expectedResult: Text remains readable, labels stay associated with controls, and the controls do not overlap, truncate critical text, or become unusable.

steps.action: Enter the prompt: 'Show 2024 warranty claims by dealer from approved views only.' and submit the request.
steps.expectedResult: The input and submit controls remain operable at 200% zoom and the request processes normally.

steps.action: Review any loading, success, warning, or access-decision message that appears after submission.
steps.expectedResult: Status text is readable, visually distinguishable from the background, and not conveyed by color alone; the user can determine whether the request was allowed and completed.

steps.action: Review the results section, including any masked or redacted values and any column headings.
steps.expectedResult: Result text, headings, and masked-value indicators remain legible and distinguishable at 200% zoom, and content is not clipped or hidden in a way that blocks understanding.

steps.action: Navigate to the audit or execution-details section while staying at 200% zoom.
steps.expectedResult: Links, buttons, and text in the traceability area remain readable and operable, and the user can access the request details without loss of functionality.

postconditions: The core governed-reporting flow remains readable and operable at 200% zoom
Critical status, results, and audit information remain visible and understandable without relying on color alone
The executed request and its audit details persist normally after the accessibility check

userStoryObject.title: As a Data Governance Administrator, I want LLM-generated reporting queries constrained by approved PostgreSQL rules so that sensitive automotive data is protected during AI-assisted reporting
userStoryObject.description:
CONTEXT & BACKGROUND:

Natural-language reporting must be governed because the platform may access sensitive automotive customer, vehicle, warranty, supplier, or dealer information stored in PostgreSQL. This story covers the guardrails that ensure LLM-driven interpretation and downstream SQL processing remain read-only, authorized, and compliant.

CURRENT STATE:

Manual or incomplete process today.

DESIRED STATE:

System supports the capability end-to-end.

KEY FUNCTIONALITY:

• Implement core logic and validation

• Expose API and UI

• Handle errors and edge cases

• Ensure data persistence and retrieval


USER INTERACTION FLOW:

1. User accesses the feature

2. User performs the required action

3. System processes the request

4. System displays results or confirmation

5. User verifies the outcome


TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS:

• Data source: application database

• Security: authentication and input validation

• Performance: meet SLA requirements


OUT OF SCOPE:

• Advanced customization (future story)


SUCCESS METRICS:

• Feature works per acceptance criteria

• No critical defects in production

Persona: Data Governance Administrator (Data Governance Administrator)
userStoryObject.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Platform constrains LLM-driven query generation to approved PostgreSQL schemas, tables, views, and read-only operations and blocks unsafe or unauthorized statements before execution

2. Platform enforces role-based access controls and masks, redacts, or excludes sensitive automotive customer and vehicle fields in accordance with GDPR, CCPA, and internal data-governance policies

3. Platform records the natural-language prompt, interpreted intent, generated SQL, access decision, and execution outcome in an audit trail that supports traceability and compliance review

4. User can I want LLM-generated reporting queries constrained by approved PostgreSQL rules so that sensitive automotive data is protected during AI-assisted reporting through the documented happy-path flow

5. System validates required inputs before completing "I want LLM-generated reporting queries constrained by approved PostgreSQL rules so that sensitive automotive data is protected during AI-assisted reporting"
